title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: 30% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted promotion lift is x2.09 (18 past events). This is deeper than prior 30% off (x2.18) but the 2026-06-29 holiday week (25% off) saw x3.1. Still, the model's uplift is well-calibrated; no need to exceed it. No evidence of over-boost.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 94.6. A 30% discount is deeper than most past promotions (avg 22.5% off), and the 2026-06-29 holiday week saw a 3.1x lift at 25% off—suggesting this 30% off could exceed that. However, the noise-adjusted promotion lift is x2.09, and the classical model’s 2.09 multiplier is already high. Back-to-school season has shown variable lift (x1.07 avg, x1.45 peak), but noise-adjusted effect is x1.0—so no additional lift. The 30% off is a strong driver, but the model’s uplift is already calibrated to past performance. No supply or closure risks. Keep multiplier near model’s suggestion but shrink slightly due to deeper discount being untested. Downside risk from post-promo dip (x0.79) is present but not triggered here.

  shelf price: 6.92 (-30.0% vs regular price 9.88)

  median 94.6 | 5%-95%: 54.1 - 217.4 | 10%-90%: 61.9 - 187.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-25% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
